findings.title: Dev rows say A3 fails on 2R, but that rests on one draw's margin at a selection level the registered rule does not use
findings.detail: The development run picked each shortlist's best at 0.5 mm; the registered rule picks it at 0.25 mm. On 2R, compaction loses A3 by one paired win (6 of 7 needed). The deciding draw is draw 2: compact s minus search s is 0.0042, and the rule needs more than b_search + b_compact = 0.0029 + 0.0040 = 0.0069. The note's own selection_error_bound for 2R is 0.25 points (draw 2's 0.5 mm gap is 0), so under the registered rule draw 2's search s could fall to about 0.0229, a margin of about 0.0067. If the 0.25 mm best also had a smaller band than 0.0029 (2R search b ranges 0.0010-0.0061), the pair flips. That gives 7 paired wins, and with 6 resolved failures compaction would be beaten on 2R. Section 4 only asks whether the selection error can rescue A1, never A3. Because every dev search s is an upper bound, the joint P(A3) = 0.23 is biased low, and expected_outcome.A3 ('expected NOT met') is firmer than the data allow. P(PASS) ≈ 0 still holds: A1 on 2R is 2 of 8, with only draw 0 inside the 0.25-point reach.
findings.evidence: Recomputed from dev_rows.json: 2R draw 2 search s 0.0254 b 0.0029, compact s 0.0296 b 0.0040; draw 6 compact 0.0139 < search 0.0165 (cannot flip). rank_stability q_spread_rel 2R ≈ 0.0025; draw-2 screen gap 0.00000.
findings.suggested_check: Solve draw 2's 2R search shortlist (8 members) at 0.25 mm, or state in the note that A3 on 2R is within selection error of flipping on one draw.

findings.title: Gated dev-row metrics and the joint OC count a draw the registered protocol would never score
findings.detail: 2R draw 1 has R_D = 1.209, outside the frozen window [1.25, 1.60]. A registered run would redraw it and never score it. It is still in the A1/A3/K1 values on the dev rows (the `mfos exp check --rows` result) and in the bootstrap, where it is resampled with probability 1/8 per slot. Neither the note nor the spec says the gated values include an out-of-window draw. Without it, 2R A1 is 2/7 and compact paired wins are 5/7, so the conclusion does not change.
findings.evidence: Independent recompute: R_D 2R = [1.290, 1.209, 1.281, 1.296, 1.406, 1.285, 1.288, 1.310]; rows carry R_D_in_window false for draw 1, yet it is included in metrics and joint_oc arrays.
findings.suggested_check: Report the gated values and the OC with out-of-window draws excluded beside the current figures.

findings.title: P(FAIL) = 0 and P(INCONCLUSIVE) = 1 are degenerate bootstrap values, reported without the caveat
findings.detail: No dev 2R search s is above 0.05 (max 0.0497; three draws lie in 0.042-0.050). The resampling therefore cannot make K1 fire, and P(K1 not fired) = 1.0 and P(FAIL) = 0 follow automatically. The runner's own oc_lower_bounds give a one-sided 95 % lower bound of 0.78 per layout on 'K1 not', so P(FAIL) could be about 0.2 or more. config.joint_operating_characteristic.values and expected_outcome.joint state 'P(INCONCLUSIVE) 1' with no note of this. The note's degeneracy caveat covers only A1 at 8/8 and 0/8. The FAIL-vs-INCONCLUSIVE split matters for founder decision 1(b).
findings.suggested_check: Report the K1 bound as an upper bound on P(FAIL) next to the plug-in value in the spec and the note.

findings.title: Small numeric misstatement of the R_D level difference
findings.detail: The note says R_D at 0.5 mm differs from R_D at 0.25 mm by at most 0.0013. Recomputed from the raw solves, the maximum is 0.00146. This has no effect on any conclusion.

findings.title: The OC method was changed in the same task that produced its numbers
findings.detail: The c_k model changed from sigma = median b / 3.92 to U(-tau, tau) with tau the GMRES tolerance. That change and the values are in one snapshot, so 'method defined before the numbers' cannot be verified. Under the old sigma (about 0.0009), c_k shifts s by about 0.1 points, which cannot move P(PASS) away from about 0. There is no material forking-path effect.

Checked the bootstrap analytically: P(Bin(8, .25) ≥ 7) = 3.8e-4 (reported 0.0003/0.0004); P(Bin(8, .75) ≥ 7) = 0.367 (reported 0.36); P(Bin(8, .5) ≥ 4) = 0.637 (reported 0.63); product 0.23 (reported P_A3 0.226). Clopper-Pearson tails at p_L = 0.688 → 0.23, and at the 2/8 upper bound of 0.59 → 0.096. All as stated.

Measured sizing: from the raw 0.25 mm result files, median walls are 925 s (2R) and 3046 s (Case 4), max peak 6.43 GB and 16.53 GB, CPU/wall about 1.4 at 2 threads. All match the claims. The W* solves converged (gmres flag 0) with tol 1.85e-5 and 2.65e-5, which equals the tau used.
Tj: Tj(W*) - Tj(W) is -1.62 K and -2.02 K, so the fallback is not due. Spearman of L1 rank vs L(0.5 mm) on 2R ranges -0.95 to 0.25 (median -0.35). Both as claimed.
Read the R_D-provisional runner change (prov_fp cleared per wave; None plus provisional flag in record mode). The logic is consistent, and the selftest asserts it on fakes.
caveats: The dev-row conclusion that A3 fails on 2R is within the 0.5 mm → 0.25 mm selection error on one draw (draw 2). A1 failing on 2R (2 of 8) is robust, so 'do not register as is' and P(PASS) ≈ 0 stand. 'A3 expected NOT met' and P(A3) = 0.23 are conservative, not firm.

The OC figures are plug-in bootstraps from 8 draws per layout. P(FAIL) = 0 and P(INCONCLUSIVE) = 1 cannot be told apart from bootstrap support limits. The runner's own Clopper-Pearson K1 bound leaves P(FAIL) up to about 0.2 per layout.
The dev-row gated values include one out-of-window draw (2R draw 1, R_D 1.209) that a registered run would redraw.
